pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis THE SMOKING GUN: Pelvic ultrasonography identifying an occult, mature cystic teratoma of the right ovary PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ectopic neural tissue within an ovarian teratoma presents NMDA receptor antigens (specifically the GluN1 subunit) to host antigen-presenting cells, breaking immune tolerance. The generated IgG antibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind directly to the GluN1 subunit of extracellular NMDA receptors in the forebrain, hippocampus, and limbic system. This binding causes receptor cross-linking and rapid endocytosis (internalization), removing functional NMDA receptors from the synaptic membrane. The selective downregulation of inhibitory GABAergic interneurons leads to unopposed dopaminergic transmission (driving early psychosis), progressive loss of forebrain motor inhibition (producing characteristic orofacial dyskinesias), and disrupted medullary control mechanisms (causing catastrophic autonomic instability and hypoventilation).
